blind_spots.why_invisible: Every candidate of the previous map asks about one note against one source. The contradiction lies between two notes, where no item reaches.

blind_spots.label: Correct content in the wrong section
blind_spots.example: The therapist's interpretation is written in the Subjective section as if it were the client's statement. The information is in the note, so coverage is full and so is fidelity.
blind_spots.why_invisible: Coverage asks whether the information is there. It does not ask where. And it was exactly the placement of items into sections that the TN-Eval experts agreed on during rubric design.

blind_spots.label: Missing what the bank never asked
blind_spots.example: In the session the client mentions stopping their medication. The question bank does not ask about medication because nobody marked it as essential. Coverage comes out at 100%.
blind_spots.why_invisible: QA measures only what it asks. The map has no item for checking the completeness of the bank itself.
blind_spots.needs: human check of the information bank; ME15

blind_spots.label: A faithful and yet harmful note
blind_spots.example: The note quotes verbatim what the client said about their daughter's sexual orientation. The quotation is accurate, supported, correctly attributed and unnecessary for the purpose of the note.
blind_spots.why_invisible: The fidelity family gives such a note full marks. The harm arises precisely through the accuracy.

blind_spots.label: A manufactured negative finding
blind_spots.example: The note says Suicidal ideation: denied. Nobody asked about it in the session.
blind_spots.why_invisible: A presence check sees a filled field. A fidelity check has nothing to compare, because the source contains neither the statement nor its denial.

blind_spots.label: Systematic inequality across clients
blind_spots.example: For clients speaking non-standard Czech the model reliably omits the content of the Assessment section. Every single note looks average.
blind_spots.why_invisible: The map has no level above one note. The inequality is visible only in a breakdown across dozens of cases.

blind_spots.label: The missing note
blind_spots.example: The model does not answer for a given session, or refuses. The note does not exist.
blind_spots.why_invisible: Every item of the map rates text. Non-existent text has no score, and if it is dropped from the denominator it raises the average of the model that failed.
blind_spots.needs: Reporting planned, usable and assessed units separately.

blind_spots.label: A citation that points correctly and does not support
blind_spots.example: A claim cites an existing turn in the transcript. The turn is about a different topic.
blind_spots.why_invisible: The validity check of the target passes. Without a separate check of semantic support this becomes a supported claim.

blind_spots.label: A note good for one purpose and unusable for another
blind_spots.example: The note is excellent for continuity: dense, professional, full of abbreviations. As a client summary it is unreadable.
blind_spots.why_invisible: A single overall quality score averages this contradiction away and hides it. That is exactly why no overall score is computed.

blind_spots.label: A note that would fit anyone
blind_spots.example: The note says the client showed anxiety, reflected on their situation and was motivated to change. Every statement is supported, nothing essential is missing, the sections fit. The same text would pass unchanged for half of the other sessions.
blind_spots.why_invisible: Fidelity, coverage, organisation and economy all give full marks. Genericness can be recognised only by comparison with the other notes of the same system, a level the map did not have.

blind_spots.label: Silent editing instead of rejection
blind_spots.example: The therapist accepts the note, but first rewrites three of its four sections. The resulting documentation is fine.
blind_spots.why_invisible: What gets rated is the final text or the acceptance. The amount of work the acceptance cost appears nowhere.

pilot_proposal.status: AI proposal; no human selection decision has been made

entries.label: Coverage of essential content, separately by importance level
entries.why: The strongest documented change against the current state and at the same time the core of the continuity purpose.
entries.human_input: A therapist must approve the information bank and assign the importance levels.
entries.risk: Without a Czech rubric with importance this is so far only a transfer of the English one. Always reported together with P14; coverage alone rewards longer text.
entries.saturation_detail: TN-Eval completeness: humans 29.5% (SD 12.4), Llama 39.7 (7.9), Mistral 38.1 (7.5). At a fifth to two fifths of the ceiling. Of all measured quantities it has the most room and nobody has hit the ceiling anywhere yet.

entries.label: Distinguishing missing information, explicit negation and not asked
entries.why: A repeatedly found weakness of our own project; without it false negative findings are manufactured.
entries.human_input: A therapist judges the disputed cases.
entries.risk: The boundary between not asked and implicit negation is unclear and will be disputed.
entries.saturation_detail: Nobody has ever measured this triad separately. There is not a single number. Our own reviews, however, repeatedly found models manufacturing the gap as a negative finding, so the phenomenon exists.

entries.label: Coverage of risk content as an undilutable layer
entries.why: The highest error consequence. Rarity is not a reason to drop it.
entries.human_input: A therapist marks the risk-related units and judges severity.
entries.risk: A rare phenomenon; in a small pilot it will have a wide interval and that must be reported.
entries.saturation_detail: Safety is the only mandatory general item in TN-Eval, but nobody reported its coverage separately. Rarity means a wide interval in a small pilot; under the protocol it is not a reason for exclusion.

entries.label: Support of claims with four outcomes and an error type
entries.why: The core of a note's credibility; the method is implemented in the project.
entries.human_input: A therapist verifies a sample of the verdicts.
entries.risk: The decomposition into claims is itself an unverified step.
entries.saturation: ceiling in sight, yet it still discriminates
entries.saturation_detail: Keren: clinicians 4.80 of 5 (SD 0.25), model 4.20 (0.49). High near the ceiling, and yet the largest effect of all three dimensions, d = 1.54. TN-Eval on a different unit: 87.0 vs 68.5 and 71.8, far from the ceiling. Saturation therefore depends on the unit, not on the construct.

entries.label: Errors in actor, time and modality as separate types
entries.why: The three-way TN-Eval typology does not distinguish these, and for psychotherapy they matter more than for general text.
entries.human_input: A therapist judges whether the distinction is meaningful in practice.
entries.risk: It may turn out that the types do not occur separately in real data.
entries.saturation_detail: Keren describe that the error type differs by component and that the model attributed interventions to the therapist that were not performed, but nobody reported these types as separate numbers.

entries.label: Placement of content in the expected section
entries.why: In TN-Eval five experts agreed perfectly on which section a rubric item belongs to (agreement during rubric design, not validation of P06 on actual notes). Placement is therefore well defined and today we do not measure it at all.
entries.human_input: A therapist confirms the section mapping for the Czech tasks.
entries.risk: Applies only to tasks with a prescribed structure.
entries.saturation_detail: The experts had PERFECT agreement on where content belongs. How often the models confuse it, however, nobody has measured. The highest ratio of measurement reliability to cost.

entries.label: Share of content-bearing sentences, always reported beside coverage
entries.why: Implemented; the main change is the ban on reporting it alone.
entries.risk: According to TN-Eval this is the dimension where automation agrees worst with humans.
entries.saturation: ceiling in sight for good models
entries.saturation_detail: TN-Eval conciseness: humans 75.6 (14.9), Llama 84.0 (12.1), Mistral 91.5 (SD 7.1). Mistral is at the ceiling and the spread narrows. Among strong models it will soon stop discriminating.

entries.label: Stigmatising wording, distinguishing quotation from the author's text
entries.why: The only attribute PDSQI introduced explicitly because of model behaviour.
entries.human_input: A therapist must approve the Czech formulations; a dictionary filter is inadmissible.
entries.risk: No support exists for Czech. The highest risk of a wrong transfer.
entries.saturation_detail: PDSQI introduced the attribute because of model behaviour but did not report the score distribution. Zero data for Czech.

entries.label: Required elements under Decree No. 444/2024 Coll.
entries.why: The only hard Czech specification we have for the audit purpose.
entries.human_input: Legal review of the conversion into criteria. The assistant is not a lawyer.
entries.risk: The presence of a field is not evidence of the correctness of its content; it must not be mixed into quality.
entries.saturation_detail: A legal criterion, not a psychometric one. A strong ceiling effect is expected: mandatory fields are either there or not, and most systems fill them.

entries.label: Taking over care: would the note carry continuation without the transcript
entries.format: yes / no / cannot decide plus justification
entries.why: The only measurement that asks directly about the purpose. Without it the whole benchmark is a proxy.
entries.human_input: Therapists as raters, trained on the instrument.
entries.risk: The most expensive pilot item. TN-Eval reports USD 190 for its whole human evaluation of notes, not for one task; P10 must be budgeted from its own procedure (measured time per note).
entries.saturation_detail: Walker asked this question but did not report its distribution. The related TN-Eval acceptance item: human notes 2.34 of 5, Llama 3.34, Mistral 3.73. Far from the ceiling and discriminates strongly.

entries.label: Acceptability of the note for practice on six parameters
entries.why: MentalCLOUDS showed that expert judgement diverges from automatic metrics; without this measurement we will not see that divergence.
entries.human_input: Therapists; the parameters must be translated and verified.
entries.risk: Five of the six parameters are not properties of the text; they must not be mixed with textual scales.
entries.saturation_detail: MentalCLOUDS used the six parameters but did not report numbers per parameter; it states only that Mistral outperformed the others and that room for improvement remains on opportunity costs and perceived effectiveness.

entries.label: Control measurement of agreement between trained and untrained raters
entries.why: Walker versus PDSQI suggests that whether the instrument works at all rests on this difference. Measuring it here is cheap and it decides the validity of everything else.
entries.risk: Requires more raters than the pilot counted on. Can be limited to a subsample.
entries.saturation_detail: Untrained raters: r = 0.07 (p = 0.270) and an inability to tell a good note from a poor one, F(3,34) = 1.15, p = 0.342. Trained: ICC 0.867 in PDSQI and ICC 0.81 / 0.71 / 0.65 in Keren. These are, however, different instruments, samples, raters and statistics: the comparison recommends training; it establishes neither its causal effect nor its size (audit A06). The size of the difference in the pilot is measured, not assumed.

entries.label: Diversity of one system's notes as an indicator of genericness
entries.unit: the set of notes of one generator
entries.why: Catches a type of failure no other proposed measurement sees: a note that is faithful, complete and well organised, and would nevertheless fit anyone.
entries.human_input: A therapist judges whether systems with low diversity really read as generic.
entries.risk: A proxy that depends on the choice of embedding model, and may be read only for notes that have passed the fidelity check.
entries.saturation: unknown, and the measure itself is fragile
entries.saturation_detail: Klein: humans had higher linguistic diversity, but the authors admit that the semantic variant changed with the embedding model chosen and gave an inconsistent picture.

entries.label: Information density and comparison at aligned length
entries.format: continuous ratio: essential information units per 100 words
entries.why: A construct in its own right, not an addendum to coverage. Without it the benchmark systematically rewards length, which is exactly the tendency models have, so the error always points one way.
entries.human_input: None beyond P01; density is computed from the same information bank. A therapist must, however, judge whether a system with higher density really reads better.
entries.risk: Comparable only among notes of the same source material. The aligned-length control condition means a second generation run, i.e. real extra cost. The differences between the two Keren studies do not isolate length; controlled length is a proposed experiment, not a documented mechanism.
entries.saturation_detail: Nobody has ever reported density. Indirect evidence: S19 aligned length between sources and humans won on preservation of salient meaning too (d = 0.70) against the authors' own hypothesis; S18 did not align length and there the models came out as more comprehensive. The difference between the studies is exactly length.

applied_criteria.detail: Preference went to a measurement resting on a source whose full text the assistant read. Ten of the entries rest on S1, S2, S6, S7, S18 or S19.

applied_criteria.criterion: Repairs a known defect of our instrument
applied_criteria.detail: P01, P02, P06 and P07 exist because a concrete discrepancy was found between what our code does and what the source it was derived from says.

applied_criteria.criterion: Every one of the four purposes has at least one measurement
applied_criteria.detail: continuity P01/P10, supervision P05/P11, client P08/P13, audit P09. Supervision and client are covered worst, because the evidence for them is the thinnest.
The development budget of the protocol: a balanced human note sample, 150 human decisions, 8 to 12 hours of human work. P10 and P11 alone consume most of the human time.

applied_criteria.criterion: At least one measurement checks the instrument, not the models
applied_criteria.detail: P12. Without it we will not learn whether the numbers from the rest of the pilot mean anything at all.

applied_criteria.criterion: A rare but serious phenomenon deliberately kept
applied_criteria.detail: P03. The protocol explicitly forbids dropping an item for rarity.

deliberately_not_used.why: The protocol forbids dropping a measurement because the models do not differ on it. A small difference can mean that all are equally bad.

CLAUDE.md: an existing implementation is not a reason to accept a criterion. That is why P06, which is not implemented, is in the pilot, and why candidate c16, which was implemented, was dropped (a decision reopened by audit A07).
Families are an organising proposal, not evidence of importance. Selection was not made by family.

left_out.reason: We have no longitudinal data. Cannot be measured.
One Czech client cluster. Cannot be measured.
Requires real clients and an ethics framework we do not have for the pilot. A proxy judgement by a professional is in P11.
Needs supervisors as raters and has the weakest evidential support of all four purposes.
Explicitly unsupported; the review found counterexamples. Measuring something without a definition would produce a meaningless number.
Not a separate measurement but a reporting rule: coverage from P01 is always reported separately per purpose and never summed. Built into the design of P01.

Half of the construct (is the relation supported?) is already in P04. The other half (is it appropriate to the purpose?) requires a purpose-specific standard we do not have; PDSQI rewards integration, which would be wrong for a client summary. Measuring it now would mean inventing a yardstick.

Measurable only against a specific reader and the pilot has no client readers. Automatic readability indices are a stand-in, not evidence of understanding. Closely related to K24, dropped for the same reason.
The plan is a type of information unit, so it falls into P01 as one of the importance levels. A separate measurement would count it twice.

left_out.candidate: K16 context of the record's creation
left_out.reason: Overlaps with P09: the Czech required elements about the author of an entry are harder and more concrete than the general professional requirement from an expired APA document.

Lacks a definition that could be operationalised, as with K15. In couple and group therapy it would be crucial, but the pilot is on individual therapy (a decision reopened by audit A07: individual therapy can also contain sensitive third-party information).
Applies only to tasks that explicitly require citations. None of the pilot tasks does, so the measurement would have an empty denominator.

left_out.candidate: K20 compliance with the task format
left_out.reason: An operational check, not a quality criterion. It runs outside the pilot as a deterministic check and is not mixed into the score.

left_out.candidate: K22 extent of the edits needed
left_out.reason: Requires a real workflow in which a therapist actually works with the draft. A laboratory pilot does not have that.

left_out.candidate: K16, K17, K18, K20, K22 as separate measurements
